messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Comparing detection probability estimates using pcount and multinomPois models
parts:
Hi Zach,

it seems you are worried about the strong difference in the estimates for p under the two models, with that of the removal model being much higher than that under the Nmix. I was wondering about the temporal scale of your sampling protocol and also about how you integrated the removal counts from the two surveys per year in the first analysis. Perhaps the removal analysis gives you mostly an estimate of "pure detection" (omitting any availability component in p). This could lead qualitatively to the observed differences.

We wrote a paper (Kery and Royle, Journal of Animal Ecology, 2010, Hierarchical modelling and estimation of abundance and population trends in metapopulation designs) where we compared multinomial and binomial mixture models for the same original data (detection histories of individual territories). This may be relevant for your study.

Also, the paper by Nichols, Conn and Thomas (EES, 2009) may be relevant, as it gives a clear overview about which components of detection (e.g., availability, strict detection) are included in the "p" of several methods for estimation of population size.

Kind regards  --  Marc

From: unma...@googlegroups.com [unma...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of Zach Ladin [za...@udel.edu]
Sent: 19 April 2013 17:54
To: unma...@googlegroups.com
Subject: [unmarked] Comparing detection probability estimates using pcount and multinomPois models

Hi there,

I am currently working on seeing how estimates of species-specific detection probabilities vary depending on analysis methods (i.e. use of N-mixture or removal models) for avian point count data collected annually with 2 visits to each of our sites per year.  For these analyses I'm only considering data from one year, and have constrained all detections to that of singing males within a 50m radius plot.  My hopes were that for species with relatively high detection probability within our study area (e.g. ACFL) that the two methods would provide similar estimates for detection, and that for species with low detection probability that either N-mixture or removal models would be better substantiated if low detection was driven by low abundance or low calling frequencies, respectively.  I thought I would post this to invite any thoughts or considerations, or if anyone notices any glaring errors in the assumptions I'm making.  Thanks in advance!

Here is an example of the code:

#removal model
> acfl_data<- read.csv("acfl_rem.csv", header=TRUE)
> y<-acfl_data[,1:4]
> site.covs<- data.frame(site =acfl_data[,5], visit=acfl_data[,6], date=acfl_data[,7],hours=acfl_data[,8],temp=acfl_data[,9],wind=acfl_data[,10])
> acfl_r <- unmarkedFrameMPois(y = y, siteCovs = site.covs, type = "removal")

> null_1 <- multinomPois(~1 ~1,acfl_r)
> null_1

Call:
multinomPois(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = acfl_r)

Abundance:
 Estimate     SE     z  P(>|z|)
   -0.545 0.0814 -6.69 2.23e-11

Detection:
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
     1.22 0.181 6.73 1.66e-11

AIC: 692.3769
 
> backTransform(null_1, type="det")

Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Detection estimate(s)

 Estimate     SE LinComb (Intercept)
    0.772 0.0319    1.22           1

Transformation: logistic

#N-mixture model

> acfl_pcount<-read.csv("acfl_pcount.csv", header=TRUE)
> acfl_data1<-data.frame(acfl_pcount[,1:2])
> visitM<-matrix(c('1','2'),132,2,byrow=TRUE)
> acfl_p<-unmarkedFramePCount(y=acfl_data1,obsCovs=list(visit=visitM) )
> null_2<-pcount(~1~1,acfl_p)
Warning message:
In pcount(~1 ~ 1, acfl_p) : K was not specified and was set to 102.

> null_2

Call:
pcount(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = acfl_p)

Abundance:
 Estimate   SE    z P(>|z|)
     1.65 1.36 1.21   0.226

Detection:
 Estimate   SE     z P(>|z|)
     -2.1 1.53 -1.37    0.17

AIC: 492.5228

> backTransform(null_2, type="det")

Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Detection estimate(s)

 Estimate    SE LinComb (Intercept)
    0.109 0.149    -2.1           1

Transformation: logistic

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Comparing detection probability estimates using pcount and multinomPois models
parts:
Hi Marc,

Thanks for your response and directing me to your paper!  Slightly different from your 2010 paper, I'm trying to apply the removal models to a 10-min point count broken into 2.5 min intervals similar to methods described in Farnsworth et al. 2002. I was using the long format with my count data set up with 4 columns corresponding to the 4 count intervals, and 1 column for visit (i.e. 1 or 2), to determine how this influences detection.   Additionally, the detection probability estimates from my first post are for each interval, so I think I'll also be needing to use the rowSums function to estimate detection for each 10-min count.  Thanks again for your thoughts!

Best wishes,
Zach
